verses.text: Behold, Yahweh’s hand is not shortened, that it can’t save; nor his ear dull, that it can’t hear.
But your iniquities have separated you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he will not hear.
For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity. Your lips have spoken lies. Your tongue mutters wickedness.
No one sues in righteousness, and no one pleads in truth. They trust in vanity, and speak lies. They conceive mischief, and give birth to iniquity.
They hatch adders’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web. He who eats of their eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper.
Their webs won’t become garments. They won’t cover themselves with their works. Their works are works of iniquity, and acts of violence are in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity. desolation and destruction are in their paths.
They don’t know the way of peace; and there is no justice in their ways. They have made crooked paths for themselves; whoever goes in them doesn’t know peace.
Therefore is justice far from us, and righteousness doesn’t overtake us. We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity.
We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among those who are strong, we are like dead men.
We all roar like bears, and moan bitterly like doves. We look for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us.
For our transgressions are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know them:
transgressing and denying Yahweh, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has fallen in the street, and uprightness can’t enter.
Yes, truth is lacking; and he who departs from evil makes himself a prey. Yahweh saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.
He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor. Therefore his own arm brought salvation to him; and his righteousness sustained him.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.
According to their deeds, he will repay as appropriate, wrath to his adversaries, recompense to his enemies; he will repay the islands their due.
So shall they fear Yahweh’s name from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come as a rushing stream, which Yahweh’s breath drives.
“A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says Yahweh.

“As for me, this is my covenant with them,” says Yahweh. “My Spirit who is on you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your offspring,  nor out of the mouth of your offspring’s offspring,” says Yahweh, “from henceforth and forever.”

footnotes.content: The Lord's arm is not short; His ear is not deaf. When we feel far from God, the distance isn't His doing—it isn't because He won't or can't reach. The very first word tells us what we most need to hear when shame makes us silent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sin builds a wall, but not because God abandons the sinner. Our rebellion creates the separation; His face is hidden by what we've done, not by His refusal to see us. Yet notice: the chapter doesn't stop here. Even hidden, He's watching—and listening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Defiled hands, lying lips, a tongue that mutters wickedness—the inventory of guilt starts small and specific. Isaiah isn't speaking to strangers; he's naming what Israel knows about itself. Honesty about our own mess is always the beginning of truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No one pleads in truth; everyone trusts in emptiness and speaks lies. When a whole people loses the habit of honest speech, justice becomes impossible. The collapse of truth in public life starts in the heart—where we stop expecting ourselves to tell the truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adder's eggs, spider's webs—the image is one of danger hatched in secret. To eat from the fruit of such deceit is to poison yourself. The nest of lies you tend will turn on you; there's no safe harbor in wickedness, even for the one who built it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The works of iniquity cannot clothe or cover you—they cannot save you. All the effort Israel has poured into crooked schemes leaves them naked and exposed. We often think our sin at least profits us; the prophet says it leaves us with nothing but violence in our hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their feet run to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are violent. Notice the hurrying—the eagerness of sinners to harm the helpless. Yet Jesus will one day stand before those who poured out innocent blood, and He will offer them pardon. Until then, the weight of such deeds is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The way of peace is unknown to them; injustice marks every path. Those who walk crooked roads don't stumble by accident—they never learned to walk straight. The path of peace is a road you must be taught; the absence of that teaching shows in your footsteps.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Justice is far from us; we grope for light and see darkness instead. The prophet shifts to the first person—no longer accusing *them*, but confessing *we*. That shift marks the turning point where Israel stops blaming others and names its own blindness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stumbling at noon as if it were twilight—the image of a people so lost they cannot see what stands in daylight. Among the strong, they are like dead men. This is not weakness; it's the deadness that comes from living in perpetual denial. Blindness leads to spiritual death.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They roar like bears, moan bitterly like doves. Israel has become a people of grief and desperation, crying out for justice and salvation that never seem to arrive. Yet God hears every cry—even the ones that feel unanswered. Waiting is not the same as abandonment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Our transgressions are multiplied before You, and our sins testify against us. Notice the preposition: *before* God, not hidden from Him. Confession means standing with your sin in full sight of the Lord, waiting to hear what He will say. This is the posture the gospel teaches.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We have transgressed and denied Yahweh, turning away, speaking oppression and revolt. The list is thorough—rebellion in doctrine, behavior, and speech. Yet even here, confession is happening. Israel cannot name its sin this clearly if something in her heart is not already turning toward repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Justice is turned backward; righteousness stands far away; truth has fallen in the street. The landscape of Israel's life has become inverted. What should stand tall is cast down. Yet a world where truth lies dead in the street is precisely the world Christ came to restore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Truth is lacking; whoever turns from evil makes himself a prey. In a world of lies, the righteous person is hunted. Yet Yahweh saw all this—the absence of justice, the persecution of the faithful—and it displeased Him. His displeasure is the prelude to His action.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor. When injustice reigns and no one steps forward to defend the helpless, God Himself becomes the Defender. His own arm brings salvation; His righteousness sustains Him. The picture of the Redeemer begins to take shape here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, a helmet of salvation on his head—the language of a warrior, an intercessor armed with justice itself. Zeal is his mantle; vengeance is his garment. Here is the God who will not tolerate the abuse of His people forever, who arrays Himself for their rescue.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: According to their deeds He will repay. His justice is not random anger; it is the precise return of what was sown. Every adversary receives recompense; every island gets its due. The God of mercy is also the God of justice, and both are one in His nature.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will fear Yahweh's name from the west and His glory from the rising of the sun. When the Lord acts, His name becomes known across all lands and ages. He comes as a rushing stream driven by His breath—unstoppable, life-giving, overwhelming in its power. The whole world sees and trembles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob. The promise is specific: the Redeemer comes to *those who turn*. Repentance opens the door; grace walks through it. Here is the hope that eclipses all of Israel's darkness—a Redeemer is coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My Spirit and my words will not depart from your mouth or your offspring's offspring forever. Readers today hear an echo: after centuries, when Jesus came to Zion, He breathed His Spirit on His disciples and sent them to speak His words to all nations. The promise is still living—it is still alive in every generation that calls on His name. As of 2026-10, we still bear witness to this covenant that will not depart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
